To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

users of micro blogging services will prefer to consume content from someone with which they are already familiar, and will prefer to consume the content which has been judged by others to be valuable.

the number of retweets and the presence of a relationship between the author of a piece of content and the user of the system is the strongest cue to influence decision making when selecting content for consumption.
When deciding to consume content from Twitter, users are influenced by the number of retweets, and by the identity of the author of the tweet, but not by the content of the tweet itself."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how people decide to read or not read content in a micro blogging system.
the question of how humans use content meta data to make decisions about which content to consume.
human content selection in micro blogging systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most effective metadata cues for content selection are: (1) the number of retweets; (2) the author’s name and (3) the author’s profile picture.

when faced with a choice of content, users prefer to consume content from someone with which they already have an established relationship, or content that has been judged by others to be of value (i.e. content that has received many retweets).
when making decisions about content selection on Twitter, users will use the cues they are most familiar with.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the recognition heuristic is applied when deciding whether to consume content, and that the most important cue is a signal of friendship.
we have shown that the recognition heuristic can be used to explain the decisions made by humans in selecting content for consumption.
the most effective way to influence a user's decision to read a tweet is to provide information about the author.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of retweets of a tweet is the most influential factor in the selection of a tweet for reading.
the metadata cues used by Twitter users in their selection of content for consumption is driven by their desire for content that is familiar to them.
when faced with a constrained decision making problem, humans will tend towards using cues representing familiarity, such as friendship information, to inform decision making.
